card.title: For Everyone’s Protection
card.instruction: Protect people by creating procedures for them. Turn concern into checklists, permissions, required steps, and increasingly narrow exceptions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written a checklist so you can safely make tea while I'm out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made tea for forty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You can initial the experience section.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cold or room temperature? I need the correct appendix.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 protects tea-making through a checklist, A3 turns long experience into an initialed section, and A5 converts a simpler drink into another appendix choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's forty years cause A3's experience signoff; B4's water alternative causes A5's temperature classification.

relationship.evidence: B2 establishes competence and B4 seeks an uncomplicated way to meet the ordinary drink need.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's simplification to narrow the protective procedure rather than allow unstructured action.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes tea-making while A is out and the safety rationale for the written checklist.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's correct-appendix question is earned by B4's new drink choice and A1's procedural artifact.
